requirement:
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> {"search_id":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","used":["1"]}. Entries
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
rationale:
The requirement fixes one structural obligation. The `finish_search` tool definition must carry the quoted description text.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_,%20D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]` is marked `{impl}` for this requirement. It builds the `FINISH_SEARCH` definition with a `description` string. I compared that string with the requirement text sentence by sentence and found them identical. The only differences are the JSON escaping of the example's quotes. The sentences covered are:
- "Close a delivered search … without an additional source read."
- The `search_id`/`used` explanation and its example.
- "Entries whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless."
- "Use used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search."
- "Every delivered search must be finished before submission."
- "The result is {search_id, finished:true}; no additional source is delivered."

The definition also gives `search_id` and `used` parameter schemas, which agree with the description. `search_id` is a uuid-formatted string and `used` is an array of strings. Both are required, and `additionalProperties` is false.

`references` shows no other implementation roots. The only other site is a `{cite}` in `md/requirements/sdk/graph/search.md`, which needs no coverage. No gaps were found and no acknowledgments were needed.
